knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Crews copy the lead's conduct, so the lead's behaviour sets the standard more than any written policy.
An unexplained exception to a rule invites a belief that the lead plays favourites. Explaining the reason keeps the rule trusted.
Specific, timely recognition tied to a result reinforces the behaviour. Generic or delayed praise does less.

practicalCriteria: The learner records three behaviours they model on shift, each with a checkable example from a real or simulated job.
The learner's recognition plan names a behaviour, a method, a cost of no more than a short message or a shared break, and a review date.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop and refer any request to skip rest breaks or safety steps to reward a crew.
Stop and refer any recognition that would involve a payment or benefit the lead is not authorised to give.
